newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Euromark volatility slides pre-U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Euromark volatility slides pre-U.S. data.

text.p: Implied volatility of Euromark options traded on LIFFE slid on Thursday, but was unlikely to fall further ahead of key U.S. data due for release on Friday, traders said.
Most activity was clustered around the 96.75 September strike, and more than 11,200 calls and more than 8,700 puts had been traded at that level by 1345 GMT.

"There's an air of prevailing calm in Europe at the moment, which seems to have stemmed from Chancellor Kohl's decision to stand for election again," said a trader at a U.S. bank here. "But there is some support from volatility from the U.S. data."

The U.S. is set to release producer price and retail sales figures on Friday, and investors are keen to see if there is anything in the data to suggest another rise in U.S. interest rates is imminent.
At the last meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee in March, the U.S. Federal Reserve added 25 basis points to the Fed funds rate, taking it to 5.5 percent.
September at-the-money options volatility was trading around 9.7 percent, down around 0.2 percent on the day, and off from 11.7 percent a week ago.
September futures were unchanged at 96.67, while December futures were down one basis point at 96.51.
In December options on the December future, volatility eased to 13.0 percent from 13.2 percent at Wednesday's settlement.

A trader at a French bank said selling straddles was popular in September, and also selling of a series of straddles in June/December/September. Again, the 96.75 strike took the lion's share of trade.

Traders said volatility in September could dip below 9.5 percent, but was likely to wait until after the U.S. data. December volatility was well-supported around the psychological level of 13.0 percent, they added.
